title: Exp-concave online optimization with one-gradient feedback and Euclidean projection
summary: Each round's loss is exp-concave with bounded gradient. After acting in the feasible domain, the learner receives one exact gradient. Public Euclidean projection supports LightONS. Regret, projection costs, and matrix-computation costs are recorded separately.

model.instance: The action set $X\subset\mathbb R^d$ is compact, convex, and contained in a Euclidean ball of radius $D/2$. Differentiable losses satisfy $$e^{-\alpha f_t(\cdot)}\ \text{on }X\text{ is concave},\qquad \|\nabla f_t(x)\|_2\le G\quad(x\in X).$$. The environment may depend on history but cannot anticipate current private randomness; the guarantee holds for every admissible realized loss sequence. Exp-concavity means that for each round $t$, the map $x\mapsto\exp(-\alpha f_t(x))$ is concave on the feasible domain. It applies to the complete action variable with the stated norm and gradient bounds.
